1911.subject: Zoology
1911.text: Recombinant DNA technology involves several steps in which initial step is of isolation of the DNA. Which enzymes are used in the process for the break down of fungal cell, plant cell and bacterial cell respectively?
1911.sol: Processes of recombinant DNA technology involves isolation of DNA of a desired DNA fragment. In order to cut the DNA with restriction enzymes, it needs to be in pure form, free from other macro molecules. The DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA along with other macromolecules such as RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and also lipids. This can be achieved by treating the bacterial cells/plant or animal tissue with enzymes such as lysozyme (bacteria), cellulase (plant cells), chitinase (fungus). The RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease whereas proteins can be removed by treatment with protease.

2223.subject: Zoology
2223.text:
Assertion : A network of food chains existing together in an ecosystem is known as a food web. 
Reason : An animal like kite cannot be a part of a food web.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
2223.sol:
The process of transfer of energy from producers through a series of organisms i.e. from primary consumers to secondary consumers to tertiary consumers by process of eating and being eaten constitute a food chain, eg. grassland ecosystem. Food chains can never occur independently in ecosystem but various food chains are inter-connected with each other forming an interlocked system known as food web. In grassland ecosystem food chains may be-
(i) Grass $\rightarrow$ Rabbit $\rightarrow$ Hawk/kite
(ii) Grass $\rightarrow$ Mouse $\rightarrow$ Snake $\rightarrow$ Kite/Hawk
(iii) Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Lizard $\rightarrow$ Kite/Hawk
So, the food web will include kite.
2223.meta: Assertion : A network of food chains existing together in an ecosystem is known as a food web. Reason : An animal like kite cannot be a part of a food web.

2754.subject: Chemistry
2754.text:
Which of the following orders are correct regarding their covalent character? i. $\mathrm{KF} < \mathrm{KI}$ ii. $\mathrm{LiF} < \mathrm{KF}$ iii. $\mathrm{SnCl}_2 < \mathrm{SnCl}_4$ iv. $\mathrm{NaCl} < \mathrm{CuCl}$
The correct option is
2754.sol:
According to Fajan rule, for covalent character, cation should be small in size and should have high positive charge and anion should be large in size and contain high negative charge.
(i) Iodine have more size than $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ so, $\mathrm{KI}>\mathrm{KF}$
(ii) $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ have more size the $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$ so, $\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF}$
(iii) $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ carry more charge than $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\text{ so, } \mathrm{SnCl}_4>\mathrm{SnCl}_2$
(iv) $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ have pseudo configuration so it has more covalent character than NaCl.
$\mathrm{CuCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}\therefore$ (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct

4961.subject: Chemistry
4961.text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
(i) $\mathrm{Li} \mathrm{NO} \mathrm{NO}_3, \mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2$ both will give $\mathrm{NO}_2$ on heatiing
(ii) $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ is less soluble in water than $\mathrm{CaSO}_4$
(iii) Alkaline earth metals do not dissolve in liquid ammonia
4961.sol:
$4 \mathrm{Li} \mathrm{NO}_3 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{Li}_2 \mathrm{O}+4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$ (anomalous behaviour)
$2 \mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{BaO}+4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$
Thus, (i) is correct.
The solubility of alkaline earth metals decreases down the group due to a decrease in hydration enthalpy compared to the lattice enthalpy.
Thus, $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ will be less soluble in water than $\mathrm{CaSO}_4$. Thus, (ii) is also correct.
Alkaline earth metals dissolve in liquid ammonia to form a coloured solution.
$\mathrm{M}+(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}) \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow\left[\mathrm{M}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_{\mathrm{x}}\right]^{2+}+2\left[\mathrm{e}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_{\mathrm{y}}\right]^{-}$
Thus, (iii) is incorrect.

5087.subject: Chemistry
5087.text: In $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.96} \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{Fe}$ is present in +2 and +3 oxidation state, what is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ in the compound?
5087.sol:
Mole fraction is unit of amount of constituent, divided by total amount of all constituents in a mixture.
Let us consider, there are ' $x$ ' molecular fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} and (0.96-x)$ molecular fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$.
Using charge conservation formula, We get, $\begin{aligned} x(+2)+(0.96-x)(+3)-2 & =0 \\
2 x-3 x+2.88-2 & =0 \\
x & =0.88
\end{aligned} $\thereforeFraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=0.88$
and fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}=0.96-0.88=0.08$
Percentage of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=\frac{0.88}{0.96} \times 100=91.6 \%$
Mole fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=\frac{0.88}{0.96}=\frac{11}{12}$
Hence, mole fraction of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ is $\frac{11}{12}$.

5088.text: Identify the incorrect statement regarding crystals having Frenkel defect.
options: Frenkel defects are observed where the difference in sizes of cations and anions is large.
The density of crystals having Frenkel defect is less than that of a pure perfect crystal.
An ionic crystal having Frenkel defect may also contain Schottky defect.
Alkali halides do not usually have Frenkel defect.
5088.sol: In Frenkel defect density remain constant. It is a defect of a cation or an anion is dislocated from its normal site to interstitial site. Interstitial site is the place between the lattice sites. This defect is observed in solids when the difference in ionic radius of two ions is very large. Hence, the density of crystals having Frenkel defect is less than that of pure perfect crystal.

5610.subject: Chemistry
5610.text: The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of two particles $A$ and $B$ is $2: 1$. If the velocities of $A$ and $B$ are $0.05 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ and $0.02 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$, respectively, then the ratio of their masses $m_A: m_B$ must be
5610.sol:
According to de-Broglie's wavelength, $\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}$ Now, de-Broglie's wavelength of particle $A$ is \lambda_A=$\frac{h}{m_A v_A}$ Similarly, de-Broglie's wavelength of particle $B$ is \lambda_B=$\frac{h}{m_B v_B}\therefore$ Ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of $A and B$ is $2: 1$ i.e., $\begin{aligned}\frac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B}$& =$\frac{h}{m_A v_A} \times \frac{m_B v_B}{h}$\\
$\frac{2}{1}$& =$\frac{h}{m_A \times 0.05} \times \frac{m_B \times 0.02}{h}$\\
$\frac{2}{1}$& =$\frac{m_B \times 0.02}{m_A \times 0.05}$\\
$\frac{2}{0.02}$& =$\frac{m_B}{m_A \times 0.05}$\\
$\frac{1}{0.01}$& =$\frac{m_B}{m_A \times 0.05} \Rightarrow \frac{m_A}{m_B}=\frac{1}{5}
\end{aligned}$ Hence, the ratio of their masses $m_A: m_B$ is $1: 5$.

5675.text: If four elements with atomic numbers $Z-2$, $Z-1, Z$ and $Z+1$ are forming isoelectronic ions, the atomic number of the ion having largest size is
5675.sol: $\because$ ' $Z$ ' represents number of protons in a nucleus. Therefore, for an isoelectronic species; size of anion > atom > cation. Means the species with more electrons w.r.t. protons in nucleus is of larger size [i.e. has smaller value of $Z$ ]. Thus, $Z-2$ has least number of protons, whereas $Z+1$ has maximum number of protons. Hence, order of size for isoelectronic species will be Z-2>Z>Z+1 Element with atomic number $Z-2$ is of largest size and option (a) is the correct answer.

\Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{t}\right) \times\left(-\frac{b^2}{a^2} \times \frac{t}{2}\right) & =-1 \Rightarrow \frac{b^2}{a^2}=2 \\
\because \quad e^2 & =1-\frac{a^2}{b^2}=1-\frac{1}{2} \quad(\because b > a) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 2 e^2 & =1
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is correct.

& =-\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{1-\tan ^2 \theta+2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan ^2 \theta}\right]-\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}(x+1)+C \\
& \therefore l=-\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{x^2-2}{x^2+2 x+2}\right]-\frac{1}{2} \tan ^{-1}(x+1)+C

10395.text: For which value of $n \in \mathbb{N}, n !$ has $13$ trailing zeros?
10395.sol:
We know in $n !$ exponent of $5$ is always less& than or equal to exponent of $2$

Hence, exponent of $5$ is equal to the number of trailing zeroes

We know, exponent of $5$ in $n !$ is given as&

$⇒ 13 = \left[\dfrac{n}{5}\right] + \left[\dfrac{n}{52}\right] + \left[\dfrac{n}{53}\right] +...$

Using $n = 57$ from the options, we get&

$= \left[\dfrac{57}{5}\right] + \left[\dfrac{57}{25}\right] + \left[\dfrac{57}{125}\right]

$= 11 + 2 + 0...$

So, in 57 !$ the power of $5$ is $13$

19562.subject: Chemistry
19562.text:
Given are the names of 4 compounds. Two of these compounds will not undergo Cannizzaro's reaction. Identify the two.
A. 2-Chlorobutanal
B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal
C. Benzaldehyde
D. 2-Phenyl ethanol
19562.sol:
Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction given by aldehydes that do not possess any $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. In the presence of a strong base, these aldehydes undergo self-oxidation and reduction to form a carboxylic acid salt and an alcohol.

Analyzing the given compounds:
A. 2-Chlorobutanal: The structure is $CH_3-CH_2-CHCl-CHO$. The carbon atom adjacent to the carbonyl group (the $\alpha$-carbon) has one hydrogen atom attached. Since it has an $\alpha$-hydrogen, it will undergo aldol condensation, not Cannizzaro reaction.

B. 2,2-Dimethylpropanal: The structure is $(CH_3)_3C-CHO$. The $\alpha$-carbon is bonded to three methyl groups and has no hydrogen atom attached. Therefore, it does not have an $\alpha$-hydrogen and will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

C. Benzaldehyde: The structure is $C_6H_5-CHO$. The carbonyl carbon is attached directly to the benzene ring. There is no $\alpha$-hydrogen atom present. Therefore, it will undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

D. 2-Phenyl ethanol: The structure is $C_6H_5-CH_2-CH_2-OH$. This is a primary alcohol, not an aldehyde. Cannizzaro reaction is specific to aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens. Thus, it will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

The compounds that will not undergo Cannizzaro reaction are 2-Chlorobutanal (A) and 2-Phenyl ethanol (D).

21321.subject: Mathematics
21321.text: Which of the following transformations reduce the differential equation $\dfrac{d z}{d x}+\dfrac{z}{x} \log z=\dfrac{z}{x^2}(\log z)^2$ into the form $\dfrac{d u}{d x}+P(x) u=Q(x)$
21321.sol:
Given the differential equation $\dfrac{dz}{dx} + \dfrac{z}{x} \log z = \dfrac{z}{x^2} (\log z)^2$.

Divide the entire equation by $z$ to obtain $\dfrac{1}{z} \dfrac{dz}{dx} + \dfrac{\log z}{x} = \dfrac{(\log z)^2}{x^2}$.

Let $v = \log z$. Then $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{z} \dfrac{dz}{dx}$.

Substituting this into the equation gives $\dfrac{dv}{dx} + \dfrac{v}{x} = \dfrac{v^2}{x^2}$.

This is a Bernoulli differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dv}{dx} + P(x)v = Q(x)v^n$ where $n=2$.

To linearize this, divide by $v^2$: $v^{-2} \dfrac{dv}{dx} + \dfrac{v^{-1}}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x^2}$.

Let $u = v^{-1} = (\log z)^{-1}$. Then $\dfrac{du}{dx} = -v^{-2} \dfrac{dv}{dx}$, which implies $v^{-2} \dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{du}{dx}$.

Substituting into the equation: $-\dfrac{du}{dx} + \dfrac{u}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x^2}$, or $\dfrac{du}{dx} - \dfrac{u}{x} = -\dfrac{1}{x^2}$.

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{du}{dx} + P(x)u = Q(x)$. Thus, the required transformation is $u = (\log z)^{-1}$.

Answer: $u=(\log z)^{-1}$

21644.subject: Mathematics
21644.sol:
The given limit is $\lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{1}{x-3} + \dfrac{9x}{27-x^3}\right]$

Using the identity $a^3 - b^3 = (a-b)(a^2+ab+b^2)$, we can write $27 - x^3 = -(x^3 - 27) = -(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)$

Substituting this into the limit expression:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{1}{x-3} - \dfrac{9x}{(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)}\right]$

Taking the common denominator:

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{x^2+3x+9-9x}{(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)}\right]$

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{x^2-6x+9}{(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)}\right]$

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{(x-3)^2}{(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)}\right]$

Since $x \to 3$, $x \neq 3$, we can cancel the common factor $(x-3)$ from the numerator and the denominator:

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 3}\left[\dfrac{x-3}{x^2+3x+9}\right]$

Substituting $x = 3$ into the simplified expression:

$= \dfrac{3-3}{3^2+3(3)+9}$

$= \dfrac{0}{27} = 0$

Answer: $0$

22190.sol:
The first line is $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) + t(-\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$. Let $\vec{a}_1 = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_1 = -\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.

The second line is $\vec{r} = (\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}) + s(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$. Let $\vec{a}_2 = \hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_2 = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.

The shortest distance $d$ between two lines $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_1 + t\vec{b}_1$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_2 + s\vec{b}_2$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2|}$.

Calculate $\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1 = (\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}) - (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = 0\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.

Calculate $\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ -1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -2 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-2 + 4) - \hat{j}(2 + 2) + \hat{k}(-2 - 1) = 2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$.

The magnitude $|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-4)^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16 + 9} = \sqrt{29}$.

The dot product $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = (0\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 4\hat{k}) \cdot (2\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) = 0 - 4 + 12 = 8$.

Therefore, $d = \dfrac{|8|}{\sqrt{29}} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{29}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{29}}$

22696.text: A proton accelerated through a potential $V$ has de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. Then, the de-Broglie wavelength of an $\alpha$-particle, when accelerated through the same potential $V$ is
22696.sol:
When a charged particle of charge $q$ is accelerated through a potential $V$, then de-Broglie wavelength is given as
$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q V}}\Rightarrow \quad \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m q}}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda_{p}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{p}}{m_{\alpha}}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{q_{p}}{q_{\alpha}}}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{p}}{4 m_{p}}} \sqrt{\frac{q_{p}}{2 q_{p}}} \quad\left[\begin{array}{c}\because m_{\alpha}=4 m_{p} \\ \text{ and } q_{\alpha}=2 q_{p}\end{array}\right]\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{8}}\Rightarrow \quad \lambda_{\alpha}=\frac{\lambda}{2 \sqrt{2}}$

22809.subject: Physics
22809.text: A bob of a simple pendulum has a mass of 4 g and a charge of $20 \mu \mathrm{C}$. If it is at rest in a uniform horizontal electric field of intensity $1000 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$, the angle that the pendulum makes with the vertical at equilibrium is:
22809.sol:
The forces acting on the bob at equilibrium are the gravitational force $mg$ acting vertically downwards, the electric force $qE$ acting horizontally, and the tension $T$ in the string.

Let $\theta$ be the angle the string makes with the vertical. At equilibrium, the forces balance as follows:

$T \sin \theta = qE$
$T \cos \theta = mg$

Dividing the two equations, we get:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{qE}{mg}$

Given values are $m = 4 \text{ g} = 4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kg}$, $q = 20 \mu \text{C} = 20 \times 10^{-6} \text{ C}$, $E = 1000 \text{ Vm}^{-1}$, and taking $g = 10 \text{ ms}^{-2}$:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{(20 \times 10^{-6}) \times 1000}{4 \times 10^{-3} \times 10}$

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{20 \times 10^{-3}}{40 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{20}{40} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $\theta = \tan^{-1} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right).

Answer: \tan ^{-1} \dfrac{1}{2}$

23367.subject: Physics
23367.text: An object is placed at a distance of $12 \mathrm{ cm}$ from a convex lens on its principal axis and a virtual image of certain size is formed. If the object is moved $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ away from the lens, a real image of the same size as that of the virtual image is formed. The focal length of the lens in $\mathrm{cm}$ is
23367.sol:
Let $f$ be the focal length of the convex lens. The object distance is $u_1 = -12 \text{ cm}$. The lens formula is $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f}$.

For the virtual image, the magnification is $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{v_1}{-12}$. Since the image is virtual, $v_1$ is negative, so $m_1$ is positive. Let the size of the object be $h$. Then the size of the image is $h_1 = |m_1| h = \left| \dfrac{v_1}{-12} \right| h = \dfrac{|v_1|}{12} h$.

When the object is moved $4 \text{ cm}$ away, the new object distance is $u_2 = -16 \text{ cm}$. The new image distance $v_2$ is positive because the image is real. The magnification is $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{v_2}{-16}$. The size of the image is $h_2 = |m_2| h = \dfrac{v_2}{16} h$.

Given $h_1 = h_2$, we have $\dfrac{|v_1|}{12} = \dfrac{v_2}{16}$, which implies $v_2 = \dfrac{16}{12} |v_1| = \dfrac{4}{3} |v_1|$. Since $v_1$ is negative, let $v_1 = -x$ where $x > 0$. Then $v_2 = \dfrac{4}{3} x$.

Using the lens formula for both cases:
Case 1: $\dfrac{1}{-x} - \dfrac{1}{-12} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{x}$
Case 2: $\dfrac{1}{4x/3} - \dfrac{1}{-16} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{16}$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{1}{f}$:
$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{16}$
$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{x}$
$\dfrac{4-3}{48} = \dfrac{3+4}{4x}$
$\dfrac{1}{48} = \dfrac{7}{4x}$
$4x = 48 \times 7 = 336 \Rightarrow x = 84$.

Substituting $x = 84$ into the first equation:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{84} = \dfrac{7-1}{84} = \dfrac{6}{84} = \dfrac{1}{14}$.

Therefore, $f = 14 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: 14

23773.text:
An electric motor raises a mass of $1.5 \mathrm{ kg}$, a distance of $1.128 \mathrm{ m}$ in time of $4.79 \mathrm{ s}$. Calculate the power to an appropriate significant figures.
(take $g=9.81 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$)
23773.sol:
The power $P$ is defined as the rate of doing work, which is given by $P = \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{mgh}{t}$.

Given values are $m = 1.5 \text{ kg}$, $g = 9.81 \text{ ms}^{-2}$, $h = 1.128 \text{ m}$, and $t = 4.79 \text{ s}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$P = \dfrac{1.5 \times 9.81 \times 1.128}{4.79}$

$P = \dfrac{16.59732}{4.79} \approx 3.465$ W.

The given values have the following significant figures: $1.5$ (2 sig figs), $1.128$ (4 sig figs), $4.79$ (3 sig figs). The result should be reported to the least number of significant figures present in the data, which is 2.

Rounding $3.465$ to two significant figures gives $3.5$ W.

Answer: 3.5 W

25392.text:
The value of the definite integral
$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{3^{\frac{x+3}{2}}}\, dx$
is
25392.sol:
Let $I = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{1}{3^x + 3} dx$

Substitute $t = 3^x$, which gives $dt = 3^x \ln 3 dx \Rightarrow dx = \dfrac{dt}{t \ln 3}$.

When $x = 0$, $t = 1$.

When $x = 2$, $t = 9$.

The integral becomes:

$I = \int_{1}^{9} \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \dfrac{dt}{t \ln 3} = \dfrac{1}{\ln 3} \int_{1}^{9} \dfrac{1}{t(t + 3)} dt$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{1}{t(t + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \int_{1}^{9} \left( \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t + 3} \right) dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} [\ln t - \ln(t + 3)]_{1}^{9}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left[ \ln\left(\dfrac{t}{t + 3}\right) \right]_{1}^{9}$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{9}{12}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \left( \ln\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) - \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \ln\left(\dfrac{3/4}{1/4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3 \ln 3} \ln 3$

$I = \dfrac{1}{3}$

28134.text:
For a reaction $A \rightarrow P$ at $T\text{ K}$, the half life $(t_{1/2})$ is plotted as a function of initial concentration $[A]_0$ of $A$ as given below.

The value of $x$ in the given figure is _______ s (Nearest integer)
28134.sol:
From the given graph, the plot of half-life $t_{1/2}$ versus initial concentration $[A]_0$ is a straight line passing through the origin.

This indicates that $t_{1/2}$ is directly proportional to $[A]_0$, which means $t_{1/2} \propto [A]_0$.

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{t_{1/2}}{[A]_0}$ is constant.

Using the coordinates from the graph, we get:

$\dfrac{240}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{x}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}}$

Solving for $x$:

$x = \dfrac{240 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3}}{4 \times 10^{-3}}$

$x = 60 \times 1.5 = 90$

The value of $x$ is $90$.

Answer: $90$

28330.text:
The instantaneous rate of disappearance of $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$ion in the following reaction is $4.56 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{Ms}^{-1}$
$2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}+10 \mathrm{I}^{-}+16 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+5 \mathrm{I}_2+8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
The rate of appearance $\mathrm{I}_2$ is :
28330.sol:
Given $-\frac{d \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}}{d t}=4.56 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{Ms}^{-1}$
From the reaction given,
$\begin{aligned}
& -\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{dMnO}_4^{-}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{4.56 \times 10^{-3}}{2} \mathrm{Ms}^{-1} \\
& -\frac{1}{2} \frac{d \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}}{d t}=\frac{1}{5} \frac{d \mathrm{I}_2}{d t} \\
& \therefore-\frac{5}{2} \frac{d \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}}{d t}=\frac{d \mathrm{I}_2}{d t}
\end{aligned}$
On substituting the given value
$\therefore \frac{d \mathrm{I}_2}{d t}=\frac{4.56 \times 10^{-3} \times 5}{2}=1.14 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{M} / \mathrm{s}$

28418.subject: Chemistry
28418.text: The following molecule acts as an :
28418.sol:
Synthetic drugs, brompheniramine (Dimetapp) act as antihistamines.

Antihistamines are drugs which treat hay fever and other allergies. Typically, people take antihistamines as an inexpensive, not patented, drug that can be bought without a prescription and relieves from nasal congestion, sneezing, or hives caused by pollen, dust mites, or animal allergy with few side effects.

We know that drugs help us diagnose and cure numerous illnesses. But any drug consumed by humans can actually have two kinds of effects - therapeutic effects and side effects. The goal is to prescribe the ideal drug, the one that only has a therapeutic effect.

34007.subject: Mathematics
34007.text: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x\right] + \left|- x + \left[x\right]\right|$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then, $f$ is
options: continuous at $x = 0$, but not continuous at $x = 1$
continuous at $x = 1$, but not continuous at $x = 0$
34007.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x\right] + \left|- x + \left[x\right]\right|$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x\right] + \left|x - \left[x\right]\right|, \left\{\text{as}\left|- A\right| = \left|A\right|\right\}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x\right] + \left|\left\{x\right\}\right|, \left\{\text{as}\left[x\right] + \left\{x\right\} = x\right\}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left[{x}^{2} - x\right] + \left\{x\right\} ( ∵ \left\{x\right\} \ge 0 )$

Now at $x = 0$, $f\left(0\right) = 0$

And $f\left({0}^{+}\right) = - 1, \left\{\text{as}{x}^{2} - x < 0\text{for}x \to {0}^{+}\right\}$

So, function is discontinuous at $x = 0$

Now at $x = 1$, $f\left(1\right) = 0$,

$f\left({1}^{+}\right) = 0 + 0 = 0$ and $f\left({1}^{-}\right) = - 1 + 1 = 0$

Hence, the function is continuous at $x = 1$.

34600.text: The number of distinct real roots of the equation, $\left|\begin{cases}cosx & sinx & sinx \\ sinx & cosx & sinx \\ sinx & sinx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$ in the interval $\left[- \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ is :
34600.sol:
Given equation $\left|\begin{cases}cosx & sinx & sinx \\ sinx & cosx & sinx \\ sinx & sinx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Performing row and column operations

${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}$

${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{3}$

$⇒\left|\begin{cases}cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx & 0 \\ 0 & cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx \\ sinx & sinx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} + {C}_{3}$

$⇒\left|\begin{cases}cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & sinx - cosx \\ sinx & sinx + cosx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding using second row, we get

$\left(sinx + cosx\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right) - sinx\left(sinx - cosx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right)\left(sinx + cosx + sinx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right)\left(2sinx + cosx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right) = 0$

$sinx = cosx ⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Or

$2sinx + cosx = 0$

$tanx = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$x = \tan^{- 1}\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Hence, $2$ solutions are there.

34638.subject: Mathematics
34638.text: Let $x = x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2y^2 \dfrac{dx}{dy} - 2xy + x^2 = 0$, $y > 1$, $x(e) = e$. Then $x(e^2)$ is equal to:
34638.sol:
The given differential equation is $2y^2 \dfrac{dx}{dy} - 2xy + x^2 = 0$.

Dividing by $2y^2$, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{x^2}{2y^2} = 0$

This is a homogeneous differential equation. Let $x = vy$, then $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = v + y \dfrac{dv}{dy}$.

Substituting these into the equation:

$v + y \dfrac{dv}{dy} - v + \dfrac{v^2}{2} = 0$

$y \dfrac{dv}{dy} = -\dfrac{v^2}{2}$

Separating the variables:

$\dfrac{dv}{v^2} = -\dfrac{dy}{2y}$

Integrating both sides:

$\int v^{-2} dv = -\dfrac{1}{2} \int \dfrac{dy}{y}$

$-\dfrac{1}{v} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \ln y - C$

Substituting $v = \dfrac{x}{y}$:

$\dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2} \ln y + C$

Given $x(e) = e$, substituting $x = e$ and $y = e$:

$\dfrac{e}{e} = \dfrac{1}{2} \ln e + C$

$1 = \dfrac{1}{2} + C \Rightarrow C = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The particular solution is:

$\dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2} \ln y + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\ln y + 1}{2}$

$x = \dfrac{2y}{\ln y + 1}$

To find $x(e^2)$, substitute $y = e^2$:

$x(e^2) = \dfrac{2e^2}{\ln(e^2) + 1} = \dfrac{2e^2}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{2}{3} e^2$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3} e^2$

35502.subject: Mathematics
35502.text: If $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right|$   $+$ constant, then $\beta - \alpha$ is equal to ______.
35502.sol:
Given,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right| + C$

Now solving $L . H . S$ we get,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - cos2x}{cos2x}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{\sqrt{2\cos^{2}x - 1}}dx$

Now let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{2{t}^{2} - 1}}$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - ln | \sqrt{2}cosx + \sqrt{cos2x} | + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|2\cos^{2}x + cos2x + 2\sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{2}cosx\right| + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|cos2x + \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{1 + cos2x}\right| + C$

Now on comparing with $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{\log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{\beta}x\right)}\right| + C$

We get, $\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}, \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \beta - \alpha = 1$

36065.text: The probability that a randomly chosen $2 \times 2$ matrix with all the entries from the set of first $10$ primes, is singular, is equal to
36065.sol:
Let $\mathrm{A}=\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{a} & \mathrm{b} \\ \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{d}\end{array}\right]$ where $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{d}$ are prime.
Total number of matrices A formed $=10^4$
Let $\mathrm{S}$ be a matrix from set of matrices $\mathrm{A}$ such that $\mathrm{S}$ is singular.
For singular matrix $|\mathrm{S}|=\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{ad}=\mathrm{bc}$
Number of singular matrices $=$ All entries are same $+$ only two prime number are used in matrix
then number of matrices with two prime numbers $=(10 \times 9) \times 2 !=180$
then number of matrices with one prime number $=10 \times 1=10$
So required probability $=\frac{10 \times 9 \times 2 !+10}{10^4}=\frac{19}{1000}=0.019$

and ${A}^{3} = - 4A$

Similarly ${A}^{4} = \left(- 4I\right)\left(- 4I\right) = {\left(- 4\right)}^{2}I$,

${A}^{5} = {\left(- 4\right)}^{2}A, {A}^{6} = {\left(- 4\right)}^{3}I$

Now $M = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}{A}^{2k} = {A}^{2} + {A}^{4} + \ldots . + {A}^{20}$

$= \left[- 4 + {\left(- 4\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 4\right)}^{3} + \ldots . + {\left(- 4\right)}^{20}\right]I$

$= - {k}_{1}I$

So $M$ is symmetric matrix

$N = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}{A}^{2k - 1} = A + {A}^{3} + \ldots \ldots + {A}^{19}$

$= A\left[1 + \left(- 4\right) + {\left(- 4\right)}^{2} + \ldots \ldots + {\left(- 4\right)}^{9}\right]$

$= {k}_{2}A$

So $N$ is skew symmetric

$⇒ {N}^{2}$ is symmetric matrix

Hence, $M{N}^{2}$ is non-identity symmetric matrix

Then the value of $\dfrac{1}{26} + \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$ is equal to
37181.sol:
We have, $a = {n}^{2}, r = \dfrac{1}{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{2}}$

${S}_{n} = \dfrac{{n}^{2}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{{\left(n + 1\right)}^{2}}} = \dfrac{{n}^{2}{\left(n + 1\right)}^{2}}{n\left(n + 2\right)}$

$= \dfrac{n\left[n\left(n + 2\right) + 1\right]}{n + 2} = {n}^{2} + \dfrac{n}{n + 2}$

$= {n}^{2} + \dfrac{n + 2 - 2}{n + 2}$ $= {n}^{2} + 1 - \dfrac{2}{n + 2} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$

From equation $\left(i\right)$,

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({n}^{2} + 1 - \dfrac{2}{n + 2} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({n}^{2} - n\right) + 2\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left(\dfrac{1}{n + 1} - \dfrac{1}{n + 2}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}{n}^{2} - \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}n + 2\left[\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) + ⋯ + \left(\dfrac{1}{51} - \dfrac{1}{52}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{50\left(51\right)\left(101\right)}{6} - \dfrac{50\left(51\right)}{2} + 2\left[\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{52}\right]$

$= \left(25\right)\left(17\right)\left(101\right) - 25\left(51\right) + \left(\dfrac{50}{52}\right)$

$= 25\left(1717 - 51\right) + \dfrac{50}{52}$ $= 25\left(1666\right) + \dfrac{25}{26}$

$= 41650 + \dfrac{25}{26}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{26} + \mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{50}\left({S}_{n} + \dfrac{2}{n + 1} - n - 1\right) = 41650 + 1 = 41651$

37887.text: A line with direction ratios $1, -1, 2$ intersects the lines $\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y}{3} = \dfrac{z+1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{-1} = \dfrac{y-2}{1} = \dfrac{z}{4}$ at the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. If the length of the line segment $PQ$ is $\alpha$, then $225\alpha^2$ is equal to:
37887.sol:
Let the coordinates of $P$ on the first line be $(2\lambda, 3\lambda, 3\lambda - 1)$.

Let the coordinates of $Q$ on the second line be $(-\mu - 1, \mu + 2, 4\mu)$.

The direction ratios of the line segment $PQ$ are proportional to $1, -1, 2$. Thus, we can write:

$\dfrac{-\mu - 1 - 2\lambda}{1} = \dfrac{\mu + 2 - 3\lambda}{-1} = \dfrac{4\mu - 3\lambda + 1}{2} = k$

This gives the system of equations:

$-\mu - 2\lambda - 1 = k$

$\mu - 3\lambda + 2 = -k$

$4\mu - 3\lambda + 1 = 2k$

Adding the first two equations gives:

$-5\lambda + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{1}{5}$

Substituting $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{5}$ into the first and third equations:

$-\mu - \dfrac{7}{5} = k \Rightarrow \mu + k = -\dfrac{7}{5}$

$4\mu + \dfrac{2}{5} = 2k \Rightarrow 2\mu - k = -\dfrac{1}{5}$

Adding these two equations gives:

$3\mu = -\dfrac{8}{5} \Rightarrow \mu = -\dfrac{8}{15}$

Substituting $\mu = -\dfrac{8}{15}$ into $\mu + k = -\dfrac{7}{5}$:

$-\dfrac{8}{15} + k = -\dfrac{21}{15} \Rightarrow k = -\dfrac{13}{15}$

The vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is $(k, -k, 2k)$. The length of the line segment $PQ$ is $\alpha = \sqrt{k^2 + (-k)^2 + (2k)^2} = \sqrt{6k^2}$.

Thus, $\alpha^2 = 6k^2 = 6 \left(-\dfrac{13}{15}\right)^2 = 6 \times \dfrac{169}{225} = \dfrac{1014}{225}$.

Therefore, $225\alpha^2 = 1014$.

Answer: $1014$

43695.subject: Physics
43695.text: A body cools from ${80}^{o}C$ to ${60}^{o}$ in $5$ minutes. The temperature for the surrounding is ${20}^{o}C$. The time it takes to cool from ${60}^{o}C$ to ${40}^{o}C$ is
43695.sol:
The formula to calculate the rate of cooling of the object is given by

$\dfrac{dT}{dt} = K\left[\dfrac{{T}_{f} + {T}_{i}}{2} - {T}_{0}\right] . . . \left(1\right)$

For the first case, it can be written, using equation (1) that

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{80 - 60}{5} & = & K\left[\dfrac{80 + 60}{2} - 20\right] \\ 4 & = & 50K . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

If $t$ is the required time for the second case, from equation (1), it can be written that

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{60 - 40}{t} & = & K\left[\dfrac{60 + 40}{2} - 20\right] \\ \dfrac{20}{t} & = & 30K . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (3) and solve to calculate the required time.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{4}{\dfrac{20}{t}} & = & \dfrac{50K}{30K} \\ & ⇒ & \dfrac{t}{5} = \dfrac{5}{3} \\ & ⇒ & t = \dfrac{25}{3}min = 500s\end{cases}$

43913.text: In a carnot engine, the temperature of reservoir is $527 ° C$ and that of sink is $200K$. If the workdone by the engine when it transfers heat from reservoir to sink is $12000kJ$, the quantity of heat absorbed by the engine from reservoir is _____ $\times {10}^{6}J$.
43913.sol:
Efficiency of Carnot engine is $η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{H}} = \dfrac{W}{Q}$, where, $Q$ is heat absorbed.

Here, ${T}_{H} = 527 + 273 = 800K$

Now, $η = 1 - \dfrac{200}{800} = \dfrac{12}{Q}$

$∴ \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{12000}{Q}$

$∴ Q = 16 \times {10}^{6}J$

46363.text: If $\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B}=\mathbf{C}$ and that $\mathbf{C}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{A}$. What is the angle between $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, if $|\mathbf{A}|=|\mathbf{C}|$ ?

Since, $\mathbf{C} \perp \mathbf{A}$, therefore

Also, $|\mathbf{C}|=|\mathbf{A}|$, therefore
$B^2=2 A^2 \Rightarrow B=\sqrt{2} A$
Now, $A^2+B^2+2 A B \cos \theta=C^2=A^2$
$\therefore \quad \cos \theta=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
This gives $\quad \theta=\frac{3 \pi}{4} \mathrm{rad}$

47393.subject: Chemistry
47393.text: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium gives significant amount of m-nitroaniline because
options: In electrophilic substitution reaction, amino group is meta directing
In strong acidic medium, aniline is present as anilinium ion.
$-\text{NH}_2$ group always directs to meta position.
m-nitroaniline has higher molar mass than o & p nitroanilines.
47393.sol:
In a strong acidic medium, aniline undergoes protonation to form the anilinium ion ($-\text{NH}_3^+$).

The $-\text{NH}_3^+$ group is strongly deactivating and meta-directing in nature.

Due to the formation of this anilinium ion, electrophilic substitution (nitration) occurs at the meta position, yielding a significant amount of m-nitroaniline (about $47\%$).

The $-\text{NH}_2$ group itself is ortho and para directing, but its protonated form directs the incoming electrophile to the meta position.

Answer: In strong acidic medium, aniline is present as anilinium ion.

48506.subject: Mathematics
48506.text: A YouTube short video is getting viral according to $f(t) = -2t^3 + 3t^2 + 5$. At what time does the video get maximum number of shares? (t$ is in hours)$
48506.sol:
Given the function $f(t) = -2t^3 + 3t^2 + 5$.

Differentiating with respect to $t$, we get:

$f'(t) = -6t^2 + 6t$

For maximum or minimum, $f'(t) = 0$:

$-6t^2 + 6t = 0$

$-6t(t - 1) = 0$

This gives $t = 0$ or $t = 1$.

Now, finding the second derivative:

$f''(t) = -12t + 6$

At $t = 0$, $f''(0) = 6 > 0$, which corresponds to a local minimum.

At $t = 1$, $f''(1) = -12(1) + 6 = -6 < 0$, which corresponds to a local maximum.

Thus, the video gets the maximum number of shares at $t = 1$.

Answer: $1$

50592.text:
An object is placed at \( 20 $\mathrm{ cm}$\) in front of a concave mirror produces three times magnified real

\( $3=\frac{-v}{20} \Rightarrowv=-$60 $\mathrm{ cm}$\)
Using mirror formula, \( $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{w}$\), we get
\( $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{-60}+\frac{1}{-20}=\frac{-1-3}{60}=\frac{-4}{60}=\frac{-1}{15}$\)
Therefore, focal length of concave mirror \( =15 $\mathrm{ cm}$\)

54232.text: A sphere of mass $m$ moving with a constant velocity $u$ hits another stationary sphere of the same mass. If $e$ is the coefficient of restitution, then the ratio of velocities of the two spheres after collision $\left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)$ will be

Conservation of momentum (gives)
$m u+0=m v_1+m v_2\Rightarrow \quad v_1+v_2=u\ldots$ (i)
Newton's experimental formula,
$v_1-v_2=-e\left[u_1-u_2\right] \text{ gives }v_1-v_2=-e u\ldots$ (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$v_1=\frac{(1-e) u}{2}v_2=\frac{(1+e) u}{2}\therefore \quad \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{1-e}{1+e}$

54818.subject: Physics
54818.text: A running man has half the kinetic energy of that of a boy of half of his mass. The man speed up $1 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$, so as the have same kinetic energy as that of a boy. The original speed of the man is
54818.sol:
The kinetic energy of moving body is equal to half the product of the mass $(m)$ of the body and the square of its speed $\left(v^2\right)$.
kinetic energy $=\frac{1}{2} \times$ mass $\times(\text{ speed })^2$
i.e., $\quad=\frac{1}{2} m v^2$
Let mass of man is $M \mathrm{~kg}$ and speed is $v$ and speed of body is $v_1$, then
$\frac{1}{2} M v^2=\frac{1}{2}\left\{\frac{1}{2} \frac{M}{2} v_1^2\right\}$  .....(i)
when man speed up by $1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, than
$v=v+1\therefore \quad \frac{1}{2} M(v+1)^2=\frac{1}{2}\left\{\frac{M}{2}\right\} \cdot v_1^2$  ....(ii)
Dividing Eqs. (i) by (ii), we get
$\frac{v^2}{(v+1)^2}=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2} v=v+1v=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

The 5d transition series consists of the elements from Lanthanum (La, atomic number 57) to Mercury (Hg, atomic number 80). This series comprises a portion of the d-block elements, specifically those wherein the d-electron shell is being filled progressively.

Elements in the 5d series span across the periodic table and are found prominently in groups commonly referred to as the transition metals. Mercury is well-known for being the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

56818.subject: Chemistry
56818.text: Which of the following reactions takes place at anode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl?
56818.sol:
During the electrolysis of molten $\text{NaCl}$, the ions present are $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$.

At the anode, oxidation takes place. The chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) migrate to the anode and lose electrons to form chlorine gas.

The reaction at the anode is:
$2\text{Cl}^-_{(l)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_{2(g)} + 2\text{e}^-$

At the cathode, reduction takes place. The sodium ions ($\text{Na}^+$) migrate to the cathode and gain electrons to form liquid sodium.

The reaction at the cathode is:
$\text{Na}^+_{(l)} + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Na}_{(l)}$

Answer: $2\text{Cl}^-_{(l)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_{2(g)} + 2\text{e}^-$

56842.subject: Chemistry
56842.text: What is percent dissociation of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ if molar conductance at zero concentration for $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{NaCl}$ and NaOH are 130,109 and $213 \mathrm{ S} \mathrm{ cm}^2 \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively and molar conductivity of $0.01 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ is $9.0 \mathrm{ S} \mathrm{ cm}^2 \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ?
56842.sol:
The percent dissociation of $\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}$ is determined using conductivity measurements. Kohlrausch's law gives the limiting molar conductivity as $\Lambda_0(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}) = \Lambda_0(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{Cl}) + \Lambda_0(\mathrm{NaOH}) - \Lambda_0(\mathrm{NaCl}) = 130 + 213 - 109 = 234\ \mathrm{S\ cm}^2\ \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ relates measured conductivity to infinite dilution: $\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_0} = \frac{9.0}{234}$. Percent dissociation is $\alpha \times 100 = \frac{900}{234} = \frac{100}{26}\%$.

This matches option D, $\frac{100}{26}\%$.

56913.subject: Chemistry
56913.text: Which of the following substances conducts electricity?
56913.sol:
- (1) Diamond: Diamond does not conduct electricity. It is an insulator because it has no free electrons or ions to carry charge. The carbon atoms in diamond form a strong covalent network, preventing the free flow of electrons.
- (2) Sulphur (solid): Sulphur in its solid form also does not conduct electricity. It is a non-metal and does not have free electrons or charged particles to facilitate conduction.
- (3) Molten $\mathrm{NaCl}:$ Molten NaCl (sodium chloride in its liquid form) conducts electricity. When NaCl is heated to its melting point, it dissociates into free sodium ( $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$) and chloride ions $\left(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\right)$, which are able to move freely and carry an electric current.
- (4) Crystalline NaCl: Crystalline NaCl (solid sodium chloride) does not conduct electricity. While it contains ions ( $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$), they are not free to move in the solid state. For conduction, the ions need to be a mobile, which happens only in the molten state

57126.subject: Chemistry
57126.text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is,
57126.sol:
The parent ring in the given structure is cyclohexane.

The substituents attached to the ring are one methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) and two ethyl groups ($-CH_2CH_3$).

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the ring must be numbered to give the lowest possible set of locants for the substituents.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the two ethyl groups, the locant set is $1, 1, 4$.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the methoxy group, the locant set is $1, 4, 4$.

Comparing the two sets, $(1, 1, 4)$ is lower than $(1, 4, 4)$ at the first point of difference. Therefore, the carbon with the two ethyl groups is designated as position $1$, and the carbon with the methoxy group is position $4$.

When writing the name, substituents are listed in alphabetical order. 'Ethyl' comes before 'methoxy' (multiplying prefixes like 'di' are ignored for alphabetization).

Thus, the correct IUPAC name is 1,1-diethyl-4-methoxycyclohexane.

Answer: 1, 1 - diethyl - 4 - methoxycyclohexane

58796.text: Calculate the radius of atom of metal forming fcc unit cell having edge length $360$ pm
58796.sol:
For a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, the atoms touch each other along the face diagonal.

The relationship between the edge length $a$ and the atomic radius $r$ is given by:

$\sqrt{2}a = 4r$

$r = \dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Given $a = 360$ pm:

$r = \dfrac{360}{2\sqrt{2}} = 90\sqrt{2}$

Using $\sqrt{2} = 1.414$:

$r = 90 \times 1.414 = 127.26$ pm

Answer: $127.26$ pm

60188.text: If the rate of increase of surface area of a spherical balloon is $5\,\text{cm}^2/\text\sec$ and rate of increase of volume of a spherical balloon is $10\,\text{cm}^3/\text\sec$, then the radius of the balloon at that time is...
60188.sol:
Let $r$ be the radius, $S$ be the surface area, and $V$ be the volume of the spherical balloon.

$S = 4\pi r^2$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 8\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 5$

$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 10$

Dividing $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$ by $\dfrac{dS}{dt}$:

$\dfrac{4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt}}{8\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt}} = \dfrac{10}{5}$

$\dfrac{r}{2} = 2$

$r = 4$ cm

Answer: $4$ cm

61635.subject: Mathematics
61635.text: If $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are inverse functions of each other and $f(x) = x + e^x$, then $g'(x) = $...
61635.sol:
Since $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are inverse functions of each other, we have $f(g(x)) = x$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x) = 1$

$g'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f'(g(x))}$

Given $f(x) = x + e^x$, differentiating with respect to $x$ gives:

$f'(x) = 1 + e^x$

Substituting $x$ with $g(x)$, we get:

$f'(g(x)) = 1 + e^{g(x)}$

Therefore, $g'(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{g(x)}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{1 + e^{g(x)}}$

61716.text: If $\mathrm{y}=x^x+x^{\frac{1}{x}}$, then $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}$ is equal to
61716.sol:
Differentiate $y = x^x + x^{1/x}$ by handling each term separately. Let $u = x^x$ and $v = x^{1/x}$, so $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{du}{dx} + \frac{dv}{dx}$.

For $u = x^x$, apply logarithmic differentiation: $\ln u = x \ln x$.
Differentiate both sides: $\frac{1}{u} \frac{du}{dx} = \ln x + 1$, so $\frac{du}{dx} = x^x(1 + \ln x)$.

For $v = x^{1/x}$, use logarithmic differentiation: $\ln v = \frac{1}{x} \ln x$.
Differentiate: $\frac{1}{v} \frac{dv}{dx} = -\frac{\ln x}{x^2} + \frac{1}{x^2} = \frac{1 - \ln x}{x^2}$, so $\frac{dv}{dx} = x^{1/x} \frac{1 - \ln x}{x^2}$.

Combine the results: $\frac{dy}{dx} = x^x(1 + \ln x) + x^{1/x} \frac{1 - \ln x}{x^2}$.

This matches option A.

(A) If $3+3=7$, then $4+3=8$.

(C) Let p : Both (A) and (B) are true $q: 5+6=17$

63190.subject: Mathematics
63190.text: The third element in the second row of adjoint of a matrix $\mathrm{A}=\left[\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}\right]_{3 \times 3} \left(\right.where \left.\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}=2 \mathrm{i}+\mathrm{j}\right)is$
63190.sol:
Adjoint element $\left(\text{adj} A\right)_{23}$ corresponds to the cofactor $C_{32}$ of matrix $A$.

Matrix $A$ with elements $a_{ij} = 2i + j$ for $i,j = 1,2,3$ yields:

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 7 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

Cofactor $C_{32} = (-1)^{3+2} M_{32} = -M_{32}$, where $M_{32}$ is the determinant of the submatrix after removing row 3 and column 2:

$M_{32} = \det\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 5 & 7 \end{bmatrix} = 3 \times 7 - 5 \times 5 = 21 - 25 = -4$

Thus, $C_{32} = -(-4) = 4$, and $\left(\text{adj} A\right)_{23} = 4$. The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

63762.text: A man takes a step forward with probability 0.4 and backwards with probability 0.6. The probability that at the end of eleven steps, he is one step away from the starting point is

Now, in 11 steps number of successes $=6$, number of failure $=5$
OR
number of successes $=5$, number of failures $=6$

& =\frac{11 !}{6 ! 5 !} p^6 q^5+\frac{11 !}{5 ! 6 !} p^5 q^6 \\
& ={ }^{11} C_6 p^5 q^5(p+q) \\
& ={ }^{11} C_6(0-4)^5(0-6)^5(1) \\
& ={ }^{11} C_6(0 \cdot 4)^5(0 \cdot 6)^5 \\
& ={ }^{11} C_6(0 \cdot 24)^5
\end{aligned}$

64405.subject: Mathematics
64405.text: The vector equation of the plane passing through the point $A(-2, 7, 5)$ and parallel to the vectors $4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is...
64405.sol:
The normal vector $\vec{n}$ to the plane is perpendicular to both the given vectors. Thus, it is given by their cross product:

$\vec{n} = (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \times (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$

$\vec{n} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 4 \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } 3 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(-1 - 3) - \hat{j}(4 - 3) + \hat{k}(4 + 1)$

$\vec{n} = -4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$

The plane passes through the point $A(-2, 7, 5)$, so its position vector is $\vec{a} = -2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.

The vector equation of the plane is given by $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{n} = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{n}$.

Calculating $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{n}$:

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{n} = (-2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) \cdot (-4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{n} = (-2)(-4) + (7)(-1) + (5)(5)$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{n} = 8 - 7 + 25 = 26$

Substituting these into the equation of the plane, we get:

$\vec{r} \cdot (-4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 26$

Answer: $\bar{r} \cdot (-4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 26$

64480.subject: Mathematics
64480.text: If the angle between the planes $x-2 y+3 z-5=0$ and $x+\alpha y+2 z+7=0$ is $\cos ^{-1}  \left(\frac{1}{14}\right)then the difference between the values of \alphais$
64480.sol:
The angle between two planes with normal vectors $\mathrm{n_1}$ and $\mathrm{n_2}$ is determined by $\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathrm{n_1}\cdot\mathrm{n_2}|}{|\mathrm{n_1}||\mathrm{n_2}|}$.

For planes $P_1: x-2y+3z-5=0$ and $P_2: x+\alpha y+2z+7=0$, their normals are $\mathrm{n_1} = \langle1,-2,3\rangle$ and $\mathrm{n_2} = \langle1,\alpha,2\rangle$.

Given $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{14}$, the dot product and magnitudes yield:

$\mathrm{n_1}\cdot\mathrm{n_2} = 7 - 2\alpha$
$|\mathrm{n_1}| = \sqrt{14}$
$|\mathrm{n_2}| = \sqrt{5+\alpha^2}$

Substituting gives $\frac{1}{14} = \frac{|7-2\alpha|}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{5+\alpha^2}}$, which simplifies to $\frac{1}{14} = \frac{(7-2\alpha)^2}{5+\alpha^2}$ after squaring.

Solving $5+\alpha^2 = 14(7-2\alpha)^2$ produces the quadratic $55\alpha^2 - 392\alpha + 681 = 0$.

Using the quadratic formula, $\alpha = \frac{392 \pm 62}{110}$, giving $\alpha = \frac{227}{55}$ and $\alpha = 3$.

The difference is $|\frac{227}{55} - 3| = \frac{62}{55}$, matching option B.

66131.text: The dielectric slab is introduced between the plates of a parallel plate charged capacitor. Which one of the following quantities will not change?
options: The potential difference between the plates.
The energy stored in the capacitor.
The electric field between the plates of a capacitor.
66131.sol:
Only the amount of charge stored in the capacitor will remain constant when the dielectric is inserted between the plates (isolated system).
Charge will redistribute, such on the plate $Q \left($1-$\frac{1}{K}\right) and \frac{Q}{K} on the dielectric interface.
The electric field present between the plates of capacitor changes because it varies with the dielectric constant:
$E^{\prime}=$\frac{Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 K}=\frac{E}{K}
The capacitance increases as:
$C^{\prime}=$\frac{K \varepsilon_0 A}{d}=$K C$
The dielectric constant also affects the potential difference as:
$$\begin{aligned}$& Q=C^{\prime} V^{\prime}=C K V^{\prime}=C V \\ & \therefore V^{\prime}=$\frac{V}{K}\end{aligned}
and the energy stored in the capacitor:
$U^{\$prime}=\frac{$$1}{2} $$\frac{Q^2}{C^{\prime}}=\frac{U}{K}$$

67545.text: The figure shows two masses ' m ' and ' M ' connected by a light string that passes through a small hole 'O' at the centre of the table. Mass ' m ' is moved round in a horizontal circle with 'O' as the centre. The frequency with which ' m ' should be revolved so that ' M ' remains stationary is (g = gravitational acceleration)
67545.sol:
Equilibrium requires that the tension force matches the weight of mass $M$: $T = Mg$.

The centripetal force for mass $m$ revolving with angular frequency $\omega$ at radius $L$ is provided by tension: $T = m \omega^2 L$.

Equating gives $Mg = m \omega^2 L$.

Substituting $\omega = 2\pi f$ yields $Mg = m (2\pi f)^2 L = 4\pi^2 m f^2 L$.

Solving for frequency: $f = \frac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\frac{Mg}{mL}}$.

67636.subject: Physics
67636.text: A current carrying circular coil of radius 'R' produces magnetic field $B_1$ at an axial point P at a distance 'x' from its centre and $B_2$ at point Q placed at its centre respectively. If $B_2 = 8B_1$, the value of x is
67636.sol:
Magnetic field at an axial point P at a distance $x$ from the centre of a circular coil of radius $R$ is given by:

$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Magnetic field at the centre Q of the coil is given by:

$B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$

Given that $B_2 = 8B_1$, substituting the expressions for $B_1$ and $B_2$:

$\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = 8 \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} \right)

\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{8R^2}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}

$(R² + x²)^{3/2} = 8R^3$

Taking the cube root on both sides:

$(R² + x²)^{1/2} = 2R$

Squaring both sides:

$R^2 + x² = 4R^2$

$x^2 = 3R^2$

$x = $\sqrt{3}$ R$

Answer: \sqrt{3}$\,R

67994.text:
For two vectors $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$, $\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q} = |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}|$
The magnitude of $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + \vec{Q}$ is ($\cos 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$) ?
67994.sol:
Given $\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q} = |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}|$

$PQ \cos \theta = PQ \sin \theta$

$\tan \theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$

The magnitude of the resultant vector $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + \vec{Q}$ is given by:

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \cos \theta}$

Substituting $\theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$:

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \cos 45^{}^{\circ}}$

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}$

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + \sqrt{2}PQ}$

Answer: $\sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + \sqrt{2}\,PQ}$

68949.subject: Physics
68949.text: A simple microscope is used to see the object first in blue light and then in red light. Due to the change from blue to red light, what is the effect on its magnifying power?
68949.sol:
The magnifying power of a simple microscope is given by $M = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$ or $M = \dfrac{D}{f}$.

The focal length of a lens is related to the refractive index by the lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right).

According to Cauchy's relation, the refractive index decreases with an increase in wavelength: $\mu = A + $\dfrac{B}{\lambda^2}.

Since the wavelength of red light is greater than that of blue light ($\lambda_{$\text{red}$} > \lambda_{$\text{blue}$}$), the refractive index for red light is less than that for blue light ($\mu_{$\text{red}$} < \mu_{$\text{blue}$}$).

Consequently, the focal length of the lens is greater for red light ($f_{$\text{red}$} > f_{$\text{blue}$}$).

Since magnifying power is inversely proportional to focal length, the magnifying power decreases when the light is changed from blue to red ($M_{$\text{red}$} < M_{$\text{blue}$}$).

Answer: decreases$

68965.text: A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 has power 3D. It is placed in a liquid of refractive index 2. The new power of the lens is
68965.sol:
The power $P$ of a lens in a medium is expressed by the lens maker's formula: $P = \left( \frac{n_{\text{lens}}}{n_{\text{medium}}} -1 \right)\left( \frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2} \right).$

Given $P_{\text{air}} = 3\, \text{D}$ with $n_{\text{lens}} = 1.5$ and $n_{\text{air}} = 1$, we solve:

$3 = \left( \frac{1.5}{1} -1 \right)\left( \frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2} \right)$,$
which simplifies to 3 = 0.5 \left( \frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2} \right)$.$
Thus, \left( \frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2} \right) =6\, \textm^{-1}$.

In liquid with n_{$\text{liquid}$$} =2$,
P_{$\text{liquid}$} = $\left( $\frac{1.5}{2} -$1\right) \cdot6 =$$ (-0.25) \cdot6 = -1.5\, \text{D}$.

The negative value implies the lens acts as a diverging lens, but among the options provided, only $1.5\, \text{D}is listed. Consequently, option C is selected as the magnitude-based answer.

69456.subject: Physics
69456.text: Applying forward bias to p-n junction, the potential barrier
69456.sol:
A forward-biased p-n junction has an external voltage applied with positive terminal to the p-side and negative terminal to the n-side, opposing the built-in potential barrier across the depletion region.

This external electric field reduces the effective potential barrier height, allowing majority carriers (holes from p-side, electrons from n-side) to cross the junction more readily, resulting in significant current flow.

Therefore, forward biasing a p-n junction decreases the potential barrier.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

69915.text: Which of the following graphs between pressure and volume of a gas correctly shows isochoric process in thermodynamics?
69915.sol:
An isochoric process is a thermodynamic process in which the volume of the gas remains constant ($V = \text{constant}$).

On a Pressure-Volume (P-V) graph, a process with constant volume is represented by a vertical line parallel to the pressure axis.

Looking at the given graphs, graph (B) shows a vertical line, indicating that the volume is constant while the pressure changes.

Therefore, graph (B) correctly represents an isochoric process.

Answer: (B)

69945.text: An ideal gas expands adiabatically, $(\gamma=1 \cdot 5)$. To reduce the r.m.s. velocity of the molecules 4 times, the gas has to be expanded
69945.sol:
The root mean square velocity is given by $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, hence $v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}$. A fourfold reduction in velocity requires $\frac{v'_{\text{rms}}}{v_{\text{rms}}} = \frac{1}{4} = \sqrt{\frac{T'}{T}}$, yielding $T' = \frac{T}{16}$ after squaring both sides. $\frac{1}{4} = \sqrt{\frac{T'}{T}}T' = \frac{T}{16}$ For adiabatic expansion with $\gamma = 1.5$, $TV^{\gamma-1}$ remains constant. Using $T_2 = \frac{T_1}{16}$: $T_1 V_1^{0.5} = \frac{T_1}{16} V_2^{0.5}\frac{V_2^{0.5}}{V_1^{0.5}} = 16\frac{V_2}{V_1} = 256$

The gas must be expanded 256 times, corresponding to option A.

70968.subject: Biology
70968.text:
Lecithin is a phospholipid made up of the following ____.
(A). glycerol
(B). fatty acids
(C). phosphate group
(D). nitrogen compound
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
70968.sol:
Lecithin is a type of phospholipid, specifically known as phosphatidylcholine, which is a major component of cell membranes.

Its structure consists of a glycerol backbone esterified with two fatty acid molecules at the first and second carbon positions.

The third carbon of the glycerol is esterified to a phosphate group.

The phosphate group is further attached to choline, which is a nitrogen-containing compound.

Thus, lecithin is composed of glycerol, fatty acids, a phosphate group, and a nitrogen compound.

All components (A), (B), (C), and (D) are present in lecithin.

Answer: (A), (B), (C) and (D).

72094.text: The r.m.s value of current in a 50 Hz A.C. circuit is 10 A. The average value of A.C. current over a cycle is
72094.sol:
The average value of a sinusoidal alternating current over a complete cycle is given by the integral of the current over one time period divided by the time period.

$I_{avg} = \dfrac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} I_{0} \sin(\omega t) dt$

Since the area under the positive half-cycle is equal and opposite to the area under the negative half-cycle, the integral evaluates to zero.

$I_{avg} = 0$

The given values of r.m.s current and frequency are not required for this calculation.

Answer: Zero

72355.subject: Physics
72355.text: A ray of light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium. The reflected and the refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. If $r$ and $r'$ are angles of reflection and refraction respectively, then the angle of incidence $i$ is equal to $[\,C$ = critical angle $]$
72355.sol:
Let the refractive index of the denser medium be $\mu_1$ and that of the rarer medium be $\mu_2$.

The critical angle $C$ is given by $\sin C = \dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}$.

According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence $i$ is equal to the angle of reflection $r$, so $i = r$.

It is given that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. From the geometry of the interface, the sum of the angle of reflection $r$ and the angle of refraction $r'$ is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

$r + r' = 90^{{}^{\circ}}$

Since $r = i$, we have $i + r' = 90^{{}^{\circ}}$, which gives $r' = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - i$.

Applying Snell's law at the interface:

$\mu_1 \sin i = \mu_2 \sin r'$

Substituting $r' = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - i$:

$\mu_1 \sin i = \mu_2 \sin(90^{{}^{\circ}} - i)$

$\mu_1 \sin i = \mu_2 \cos i$

$\dfrac{\sin i}{\cos i} = \dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}$

$\tan i = \sin C$

$i = \tan^{-1}(\sin C)$

Answer: $\tan^{-1}(\sin C)$

74654.subject: General Ability
74654.text:
The sun is observed to be reddish when it is near the horizon,
i.e., in the morning and the evening. This is because
options: red light is least scattered by atmosphere
red light is most scattered by atmosphere
it is the colour of the Sun in the morning and evening
74654.sol:
Tiny molecules in our atmosphere cause light to scatter. That's why our sky looks blue: it's because the atmosphere scatters the bluish component of white sunlight. And it's why the sun looks reddish when it's near the horizon. Sunlight encounters more air molecules when the sun is low in the sky than when the sun is overhead. Even more blue light is scattered away, leaving mostly the reddish scattering
$\propto \frac{1}{\lambda^4}$ component of white sunlight to travel the straighter path to your eyes. So the setting and rising sun looks red.

The hypocentre is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts. It is also commonly termed the focus.

It is the exact location where the strain energy stored in the rock is first released, marking the origin of the seismic waves.

This point can be located at various depths beneath the Earth's surface, ranging from near the surface to hundreds of kilometers deep.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

76364.subject: Mathematics
76364.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

Consider the following statements:
I. $f(x)$ is an increasing function.
II. $f(x)$ has local maximum at $x = 0$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76364.sol:
Given $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $f'(x) = 2x$.

For $x < 0$, $f'(x) < 0$, which means $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing in $(-\infty, 0)$.

For $x > 0$, $f'(x) > 0$, which means $f(x)$ is strictly increasing in $(0, \infty)$.

Since $f(x)$ is not increasing on its entire domain, Statement I is incorrect.

To find local extrema, we set $f'(x) = 0$, which gives $x = 0$.

The second derivative is $f''(x) = 2$.

Since $f''(0) = 2 > 0$, $f(x)$ has a local minimum at $x = 0$, not a local maximum.

Thus, Statement II is also incorrect.

Both statements are incorrect.

Answer: Neither I nor II

$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Latus rectum }=\frac{2 b^2}{a} \\ & \text{minor axis }=2 b \\ & \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \frac{2 b^2}{a} & =\frac{1}{2} \times 2 b \\ \Rightarrow \quad b & =\frac{2 b^2}{a} \\ \Rightarrow \quad a & =2 b\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$

e^2 & =\frac{3}{4} \\

\end{aligned}$

79851.subject: Botany
79851.sol:
• The cells remain in an inert state in the G0 phase of the cell cycle. Hence, G0 can be either viewed as the distinct inert stage which occurs outside the cell cycle or as an extension to the G1 phase, where cell neither divides nor prepares for it.
  • Sometimes, G0 is also referred to as “post-mitotic” state where cells in G0 are in non-dividing phase in the outside of cell cycle.
  • Some types of cells, such as nerve and heart muscle cells, become post-mitotic when they reach maturity (i.e., when they are terminally differentiated) but continue to perform their main functions for the rest of the organism's life.
  • Multinucleated muscle cells which don’t undergo cytokinesis are also thought to be in the G0 stage. Hence, it suspends the cell cycle.
  • G0 stage represents actually indicates the arrest of cell cycle and onset of differentiation.

83123.subject: Physics
83123.text: A particle moves so that its position vector is given by $\overset{\to}{r} = cos\omegat\overset{^}{x} + sin\omegat\overset{^}{y}$, where $\omega$ is a constant. Which of the following is true?
options: Velocity and acceleration both are perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{r}$.
Velocity and acceleration both are parallel to $\overset{\to}{r}$.
Velocity is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{r}$ and acceleration is directed towards the origin.
Velocity is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{r}$ and acceleration is directed away from the origin.
83123.sol:
Position vector is, $\overset{\to}{r} = cos ⁡ \omega t \overset{^}{x} + sin ⁡ \omega t \overset{^}{y}$

Velocity of particle is $\overset{\to}{v} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{r}}{dt}$

$\overset{\to}{v} = -sin \omega t \times \omega\overset{^}{x} + cos \omegat \times \omega\overset{^}{y}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = \omega\left(- sin \omegat\overset{^}{x} + cos \omegat\overset{^}{y}\right)$

Acceleration of the particle is

$\overset{\to}{a} = \dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = - {\omega}^{2}\left(cos \omegat\overset{^}{x} + sin \omegat\overset{^}{y}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} = - {\omega}^{2}\overset{\to}{r}$ ,

So direction of $\overset{\to}{r}$ and $\overset{\to}{a}$ are opposite.

As $\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} = 0 ⇒ \overset{\to}{v} ⊥ \overset{\to}{a}$ and

$\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{\to}{r} = 0 ⇒ \overset{\to}{v} ⊥ \overset{\to}{r}$,

So, velocity is perpendicular to $\overset{\to}{r}$ and acceleration is directed towards the origin.

83480.subject: Physics
83480.text: An ideal Zener diode with breakdown voltage of $-3$ V is reverse biased with a negative input voltage $V_i=-5$ V. The magnitude of voltage difference between points $B$ and $A$ is :
83480.sol:
Given that the Zener diode is reverse biased with an input voltage of magnitude $|V_i| = 5$ V.

The breakdown voltage of the ideal Zener diode is $|V_Z| = 3$ V.

Since the applied voltage is greater than the Zener breakdown voltage ($5$ V $> 3$ V), the Zener diode operates in the breakdown region.

In the breakdown region, the voltage drop across the ideal Zener diode remains constant at its breakdown voltage. Therefore, the potential difference between points $C$ and $B$ is $V_{CB} = 3$ V.

The total voltage is applied across the series combination of the Zener diode and the resistor $R$. By Kirchhoff's Voltage Law, the sum of the voltage drops across the Zener diode and the resistor equals the total applied voltage.

Let $V_{BA}$ be the voltage difference between points $B$ and $A$, which is the voltage across the resistor $R$.

$|V_i| = V_{CB} + V_{BA}$

$5 = 3 + V_{BA}$

$V_{BA} = 2$ V.

The magnitude of the voltage difference between points $B$ and $A$ is $2$ V.

Answer: $2$ V

84366.subject: Zoology
84366.text: Random genetic drift in a population probably results from:
84366.sol:
Genetic drift (Sewall Wright effect) is the random change in the frequency of alleles in a population over successive generations in the gametes. Each new generation differs from its parental generation with regard to allele frequencies simply because of random variation in the distribution of gametes. This process is more rapid in smaller populations, or when the alleles concerned confer no apparent benefit compared to their counterparts.
Related Theory
A founder effect occurs when a new colony is started by a few members of the original population. This small population size means that the colony may have reduced genetic variation from the original population and a non-random sample of the genes in the original population.

84957.sol:
In DNA molecule the adjacent deoxyribonucleotides are joined in a chain by phosphodiester bridges or bonds, which link the $5^{\prime}$ carbon of deoxyribose of one mononucleotide unit with 3 carbon of deoxyribose of next mononucleotide unit. According to Watson and Crick DNA molecule consists of two such polynucleotide chains wrapped helically around each other, with the sugar phosphate chain on the outside and purine and pyrimidine on the inside of helix. The two strands run antiparallely, ie, one strand has phosphodiester linkage in $3 \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ direction while other strand has phosphodiester linkage in $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3$ direction.

86620.subject: Mathematics
86620.text: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f''(x) = -f(x)$. Let $h : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $h'(x) = f(x)^2 + (f'(x))^2$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. If $h(0) = 1$ and $h\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}$, then the value of $h(100)$ is
86620.sol:
Given $f''(x) = -f(x)$

Multiplying both sides by $2f'(x)$:

$2f'(x)f''(x) + 2f(x)f'(x) = 0$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$(f'(x))^2 + (f(x))^2 = C$, where $C$ is a constant.

Given $h'(x) = (f(x))^2 + (f'(x))^2$

$h'(x) = C$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$h(x) = Cx + D$, where $D$ is a constant.

Given $h(0) = 1$, we get $D = 1$.

Given $h\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}$, we get:

$C\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + 1 = \dfrac{5}{3} \Rightarrow C = 2$

Thus, $h(x) = 2x + 1$.

For $x = 100$:

$h(100) = 2(100) + 1 = 201$

Answer: $201$

then $c + d = 5$

$= \dfrac{\text{E} + \text{E}}{{r}_{1} + {r}_{2} + \text{R}} = \dfrac{2\text{E}}{{r}_{1} + {r}_{2} + \text{R}}$

Potential difference across first cell = $\text{E} - {ir}_{1}$

$= \text{E} - \dfrac{2\text{E} \times {r}_{1}}{\left({r}_{1} + {r}_{2}\right) + \text{R}}$

The acceleration of the electron is

The velocity of the electron as a function of time is

$v = at = \dfrac{eE}{m}t$

The de-Broglie wavelength is

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m\left(\dfrac{eE}{m}\right)t}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{eEt}$
$\dfrac{d\lambda}{dt} = - \dfrac{h}{eEt^{2}}$

100497.text: A ball is thrown at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. If its speed at the maximum height is $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, what is its initial speed of projection?
100497.sol:
At the highest point of a projectile's trajectory, the vertical component of velocity is zero. The speed at this point is entirely due to the horizontal component of the initial velocity, which remains constant throughout the motion.

Let the initial speed be $u$. The speed at the maximum height is given by:
$v = u \cos \theta$

Given that $v = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\theta = 60^{\circ}$:
$15 = u \cos 60^{\circ}$
$15 = u \times \dfrac{1}{2}$
$u = 30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Answer: $30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Wheel A attains a rotational speed of $600\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ s}$, while wheel B attains a rotational speed of $900\text{ rpm}$ in $12\text{ s}$. The ratio of the angular acceleration of wheel A to that of wheel B is
101204.sol:
Let $\alpha_A$ and $\alpha_B$ be the angular accelerations of wheels A and B respectively.

Since both start from rest, the angular acceleration is given by $\alpha = \dfrac{\Delta\omega}{\Delta t}$.

For wheel A: $\omega_A = 600\text{ rpm}$, $t_A = 10\text{ s}$.
$\alpha_A \propto \dfrac{600}{10} = 60$

For wheel B: $\omega_B = 900\text{ rpm}$, $t_B = 12\text{ s}$.
$\alpha_B \propto \dfrac{900}{12} = 75$

The ratio of their angular accelerations is:
$\dfrac{\alpha_A}{\alpha_B} = \dfrac{60}{75} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

The conversion factor from $\text{rpm}$ to $\text{rad s}^{-1}$ cancels out in the ratio.

Answer: $4:5$

103347.subject: Physics
103347.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Infinite L-section ladder)List-II (Equivalent resistance)
(A) Series $1\ \Omega$, Shunt $2\ \Omega$(I) $2\ \Omega$
(B) Series $2\ \Omega$, Shunt $4\ \Omega$(II) $4\ \Omega$
(C) Series $3\ \Omega$, Shunt $18\ \Omega$(III) $9\ \Omega$
(D) Series $4\ \Omega$, Shunt $12\ \Omega$(IV) $8\ \Omega$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103347.sol:
For an infinite L-section ladder with series resistance $R_s$ and shunt resistance $R_{sh}$, the equivalent resistance $R$ is given by:
$R = R_s + \dfrac{R_{sh} R}{R_{sh} + R}$
$\Rightarrow R(R_{sh} + R) = R_s(R_{sh} + R) + R_{sh} R$
$\Rightarrow R^2 - R_s R - R_s R_{sh} = 0$

For (A): $R_s = 1\ \Omega$, $R_{sh} = 2\ \Omega$
$R^2 - R - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow (R - 2)(R + 1) = 0 \Rightarrow R = 2\ \Omega$. So, (A) matches with (I).

For (B): $R_s = 2\ \Omega$, $R_{sh} = 4\ \Omega$
$R^2 - 2R - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow (R - 4)(R + 2) = 0 \Rightarrow R = 4\ \Omega$. So, (B) matches with (II).

For (C): $R_s = 3\ \Omega$, $R_{sh} = 18\ \Omega$
$R^2 - 3R - 54 = 0 \Rightarrow (R - 9)(R + 6) = 0 \Rightarrow R = 9\ \Omega$. So, (C) matches with (III).

For (D): $R_s = 4\ \Omega$, $R_{sh} = 12\ \Omega$
$R^2 - 4R - 48 = 0 \Rightarrow (R - 8)(R + 6) = 0 \Rightarrow R = 8\ \Omega$. So, (D) matches with (IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

103533.text: Three magnetic materials $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ have magnetic susceptibilities ($\chi$) of $-0.004$, $2.4 \times 10^{-5}$, and $3000$ respectively. The magnetic nature of $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ respectively is:
103533.sol:
For material $X$, $\chi = -0.004$. Since $-1 \le \chi < 0$, it is a diamagnetic material.

For material $Y$, $\chi = 2.4 \times 10^{-5}$. Since $0 < \chi < \varepsilon$ (a small positive number), it is a paramagnetic material.

For material $Z$, $\chi = 3000$. Since $\chi \gg 1$, it is a ferromagnetic material.

Thus, the correct sequence is Diamagnetic, Paramagnetic, Ferromagnetic.

Answer: Diamagnetic, Paramagnetic, Ferromagnetic

103721.subject: Physics
103721.text: Two identical coaxial circular loops, each of radius $R$, are placed at a separation of $2R$. If both loops carry the same current $I$ in the same direction, the magnitude of the net magnetic field at the exact midpoint of their common axis is:
103721.sol:
Let the two loops be placed coaxially with a separation of $2R$. The midpoint of their common axis is at a distance $x = R$ from the centre of each loop.

The magnetic field produced by one loop at a distance $x$ on its axis is given by:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Substituting $x = R$:
$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2\sqrt{2}R^3)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}R}$

Since the currents in both loops flow in the same direction, the magnetic fields produced by them at the midpoint point in the same direction.

By the principle of superposition, the net magnetic field is the sum of the individual fields:
$B_{\text{net}} = B_1 + B_2 = 2B_1$

$B_{\text{net}} = 2 \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}R} \right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\sqrt{2}R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\sqrt{2}R}$

104273.subject: Physics
104273.text:
The magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave travelling in a transparent medium is given by:
$B_y = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ T}$
The corresponding expression for the electric field vector is:
104273.sol:
From the given magnetic field equation, $B_y = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ T}$, we can extract:
Wave number, $k = 10^3 \text{ rad/m}$
Angular frequency, $\omega = 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ rad/s}$
Magnetic field amplitude, $B_0 = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}$

The speed of the wave in the medium is:
$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{11}}{10^3} = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

The amplitude of the electric field is:
$E_0 = v B_0 = (2 \times 10^8) \times (2 \times 10^{-8}) = 4 \text{ V/m}$

The phase argument $(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t)$ indicates that the wave propagates in the $+z$ direction ($\hat{v} = \hat{k}$).
The magnetic field is in the $+y$ direction ($\hat{B} = \hat{j}$).
The direction of propagation is given by the cross product $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v}$.
We need $\hat{E} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$.
Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, the electric field must oscillate in the $+x$ direction ($\hat{i}$).

Therefore, the electric field vector is:
$E_x = 4 \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ V/m}$

Answer: $E_x = 4 \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ V/m}$

104368.subject: Physics
104368.text:
Assertion (A) Propagation of light through an optical fibre is due to total internal reflection taking place at the core-clad interface.
Reason (R) Refractive index of the material of the core of the optical fibre is greater than that of air.
options: both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
104368.sol:
Assertion and Reason Analysis
- Assertion (A): The assertion states that light propagation through an optical fiber is due to total internal reflection (TIR) at the core-clad interface. This is true. Light entering the fiber's core strikes the boundary between the core and the cladding at an angle greater than the critical angle, causing the light to reflect back into the core rather than refracting out. This process repeats, allowing light to travel long distances inside the fiber.
- Reason (R): The reason states that the refractive index of the optical fiber's core is greater than that of air. This is also true. The core is a glass or plastic material with a refractive index typically around 1.5, while air has a refractive index of approximately 1.0.
Conclusion
Both the assertion and the reason are true statements. However, the reason is not a correct explanation for the assertion. For TIR to occur, the light must travel from a denser medium (higher refractive index) to a rarer medium (lower refractive index). The relevant interface is between the core and the cladding, where the core's refractive index is greater than the cladding's. The relationship between the core's refractive index and air's refractive index is not directly responsible for the TIR phenomenon within the fiber itself.
Therefore, the correct option is (2): both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

104686.subject: Physics
104686.text: Two light waves represented by $y_1 = a \sin(\omega_1 t - k_1 x)$ and $y_2 = a \sin(\omega_2 t - k_2 x + \phi_0)$ arrive at a point P on a screen. It is observed that a sustained (steady) interference pattern is formed on the screen. For this sustained pattern to exist, what must be the primary condition regarding the phase difference ($\Delta\phi$) between the two waves at point P?
options: $\Delta\phi$ must be an integer multiple of $2\pi$
104686.sol:
For a sustained (steady) interference pattern to be observed, the positions of maxima and minima on the screen must not shift over time.

The resultant intensity at any point depends on the phase difference $\Delta\phi$ between the interfering waves. If $\Delta\phi$ changes with time, the intensity at point P will fluctuate rapidly, resulting in a uniform average illumination rather than a steady pattern.

Therefore, the fundamental requirement for sustained interference (coherence) is that the phase difference $\Delta\phi$ between the two waves must remain constant with respect to time (i.e., independent of time). This implies that the angular frequencies must be equal ($\omega_1 = \omega_2$).

Options stating $\Delta\phi$ must be zero or an integer multiple of $2\pi$ are conditions for constructive interference (maxima) specifically, not the general requirement for the entire sustained pattern.

Answer: $\Delta\phi$ must be independent of time

Match List-I with List-II regarding the least count of various measuring instruments.

List-I (Instrument Configuration)List-II (Least Count)
(A) Screw gauge: Pitch $1\text{ mm}$, $100$ circular divisions(I) $0.02\text{ mm}$
(B) Screw gauge: Pitch $0.5\text{ mm}$, $100$ circular divisions(II) $0.1\text{ mm}$
(C) Vernier caliper: $1\text{ MSD} = 1\text{ mm}$, $10\text{ VSD} = 9\text{ MSD}$(III) $0.01\text{ mm}$
(D) Vernier caliper: $1\text{ MSD} = 1\text{ mm}$, $50\text{ VSD} = 49\text{ MSD}$(IV) $0.005\text{ mm}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
105430.sol:
For a screw gauge, Least Count (LC) = $\dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of circular divisions}}$

(A) $\text{LC} = \dfrac{1\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.01\text{ mm}$. This matches (III).

(B) $\text{LC} = \dfrac{0.5\text{ mm}}{100} = 0.005\text{ mm}$. This matches (IV).

For a Vernier caliper, Least Count (LC) = $1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD}$

(C) $10\text{ VSD} = 9\text{ MSD} \Rightarrow 1\text{ VSD} = 0.9\text{ MSD}$.
$\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - 0.9\text{ MSD} = 0.1\text{ MSD}$. Since $1\text{ MSD} = 1\text{ mm}$, $\text{LC} = 0.1\text{ mm}$. This matches (II).

(D) $50\text{ VSD} = 49\text{ MSD} \Rightarrow 1\text{ VSD} = \dfrac{49}{50}\text{ MSD}$.
$\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - \dfrac{49}{50}\text{ MSD} = \dfrac{1}{50}\text{ MSD} = 0.02\text{ mm}$. This matches (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
